title: Bridge and Harbor
premise: In the harbor city of Saltmere, 1919, Wendell Vane — a pearl diver's son indentured to the Corvane Trading Company since childhood — has survived seven years by learning which silences keep people safe. When a sealed letter arrives naming his family as conspirators in a smuggling plot tied to the unfinished armistice, Wendell is forced to choose between the company that owns his papers and a promise he made in peacetime to Ilse Marchetti, now declared an enemy of the state. As investigators close in and old debts surface, Wendell discovers the letter was bait, planted by someone inside Corvane who needs a scapegoat. In the end, Wendell trades his own freedom for Ilse's escape on the last neutral ship out of the harbor, keeping his promise at the price of everything else — and learns that memory, unlike contracts, cannot be seized.
about_author: August Kavanagh is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing port ledgers and intercepted letters from the postwar years. Bridge and Harbor is their second novel, drawn from the silences between official records.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Opening in the Corvane counting house, where Wendell catalogs pearls he'll never own and practices the silences that have kept him alive for seven years. A routine delivery brings him face to face with Mr. Aldous Corvane himself, who studies him too long. Emotional beat: the quiet dread of being noticed.

chapters.title: A Letter, Sealed
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A courier delivers a sealed letter addressed not to Corvane but to 'the Vane family' — a name Wendell hasn't heard spoken aloud in years. He hides it inside his boot, heart hammering through the afternoon inventory. Emotional beat: terror wrapped in curiosity; the past knocking.

chapters.title: What the Diver's Daughter Knew
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV, seven years earlier. A flashback to the peacetime summer when Wendell promised Ilse Marchetti he would come for her if she ever needed him, sealing it with a pearl from her father's last dive. Emotional beat: warmth and innocence, establishing the promise's weight before its cost appears.

chapters.title: Names on Paper
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Unable to resist, Wendell steams the letter open: it names his family among suppliers to a wartime smuggling ring still operating under armistice cover. The handwriting is half-familiar. He burns it but memorizes every word. Emotional beat: the moment silence stops being safety and becomes complicity.

chapters.title: The Company Keeps Its Own
chapters.summary: Mr. Corvane's POV. Corvane reviews his ledger of debts and favors, revealing he knows more about Wendell's parentage than Wendell suspects. He orders the boy watched, calling him 'an investment.' Emotional beat: cold paternalism; the reader sees the trap being built.

chapters.title: Salt in the Wound
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell visits the old diving quarter and finds his mother's former neighbor, Maren, who confirms the letter's claims are true — his father did run cargo during the war, to feed the family. Emotional beat: grief reframing shame into survival, the theme of inheritance made flesh.

chapters.title: An Enemy by Declaration
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. News spreads that the Marchetti name has been added to an enemy registry pending the final armistice terms. Wendell realizes Ilse is trapped in the city, her family's warehouse under seal. Emotional beat: urgency colliding with fear; the promise stirs awake.

chapters.title: The Watcher at the Gate
chapters.summary: Tobias Grell's POV. Grell, Corvane's hired watcher, follows Wendell to the sealed Marchetti warehouse and reports back — but omits one detail, for reasons of his own. Emotional beat: menace with a crack of ambiguity; even predators hedge.

chapters.title: Through the Sealed Door
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. At night, Wendell slips into the warehouse through the loading bridge and finds Ilse living among crated memories of her father's trade. Their reunion is wary, tender, and interrupted by a patrol's lanterns outside. Emotional beat: love rekindled under threat; the promise becomes actionable.

chapters.title: Terms Not Yet Signed
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse explains the armistice is stalled — enemy status is provisional, revocable, weaponizable. She believes someone at Corvane engineered the letter to force her family's assets to auction. Emotional beat: sharpening resolve; suspicion acquires a shape.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A second letter arrives, this one demanding Wendell deliver Corvane's shipping codes within a week or the Vane name goes to the magistrates. The handwriting matches the first. Someone wants him turned traitor either way. Emotional beat: claustrophobia; every exit is a door into another room.

chapters.title: Maren's Ledger
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren reveals she kept her own accounts of the war years — including which Corvane clerk forged the Vane entries. She gives Wendell the page but warns him: paper doesn't protect people, people protect paper. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; the cost of truth acknowledged.

chapters.title: Grell's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tobias Grell's POV. Grell corners Wendell and offers to lose him in the crowds for a price: the pearl Wendell carries, the one from the promise. Wendell refuses. Emotional beat: defiance hardening into identity; what he keeps is who he is.

chapters.title: The Auction Notice
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The Marchetti warehouse is posted for auction in nine days — timed exactly to Wendell's deadline. He understands at last: the letter-writer needs both the codes and the scapegoat before the armistice makes enemy seizures illegal. Emotional beat: clarity arriving like cold water; the clock starts.

chapters.title: What Silences Cost
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell confronts the forger, junior clerk Edmund Hale, who breaks down and admits he was coerced by someone above him — but flees before naming them, leaving his confession unsigned. Emotional beat: hope raised and dashed; cowardice as tragedy.

chapters.title: Night on the Loading Bridge
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse and Wendell plan her escape aboard the Meridian, a neutral ship departing the night before the auction. Wendell insists on coming; she refuses to let him burn his life for hers. They quarrel, then hold each other in the dark. Emotional beat: love arguing with sacrifice.

chapters.title: Corvane's Study
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell breaks into Corvane's study seeking proof and finds it: correspondence showing Corvane himself orchestrated the letters, using Wendell's family history as leverage to seize the Marchetti holdings before the armistice forecloses him. Emotional beat: betrayal confirmed; the master revealed as merely desperate.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Tobias Grell's POV. Grell catches Wendell leaving the study. Instead of turning him in, Grell demands the codes — revealing he was the leak Corvane feared all along. Wendell hands over false pages bought from Maren's contacts. Emotional beat: high-wire deception; survival by sleight of hand.

chapters.title: The Armistice Is Signed — Or Isn't
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. On auction morning, word races through the city: the final armistice terms are signed, enemy seizures are void — or are they? Conflicting reports paralyze the magistrates. Corvane forces the auction anyway. Emotional beat: chaos as both shield and blade.

chapters.title: Bridge and Harbor
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Climax. Wendell publicly presents Maren's ledger and Hale's unsigned confession at the auction floor, accusing Corvane of forgery before the assembled buyers and a magistrate. Corvane counters by exposing Wendell's theft of the study documents. Both men fall together. Emotional beat: the price paid in full; truth as mutual destruction.

chapters.title: The Last Neutral Ship
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. With charges pending against him and Corvane ruined, Wendell uses the confusion to reach the Meridian. Ilse waits at the gangway. He gives her the pearl and stays behind — the promise kept, the debt honored, the harbor closing behind her. Emotional beat: bittersweet fulfillment; love measured in what is given up.

chapters.title: Which Silences Keep People Safe
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, epilogue. Months later, cleared by the magistrate's inquiry, Wendell returns to the diving quarter and takes up his father's trade, free of Corvane's papers at last. He writes letters he may never send and keeps one pearl in his pocket. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; memory as inheritance, silence finally chosen rather than imposed.
